A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amplification of the HER oncogene is not a common event in human BC, but the LOH at 11p and at 17p is frequently observed.
LOH at chromosome 17 is a common event in BC and that it occurs independently of other genetic alterations studied, with the only exception of HER‐2 amplifications.
LOH at 11p and 17q was found in 27 and 29% of cases respectively, while that for 17p was found in 46% of cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amplification of HER‐2 oncogenes and the LOH at chromosome 17 in BC are not random events, but are closely related to the clinical characteristics of tumours and to each other.
the presence of LOH at chromosome 17 is not a universal marker of BC malignancy and that the association between LOH at 11p and 17q and HER‐2 amplifications should be considered with caution.
the amplification of HER‐2 gene is not the sole factor determining the aggressiveness of BC.
